posts.title: Does it Not?
posts.description: Nowhere in the Bible does it say “Go to church.” That’s probably not the big zinger/ argument winner some people might think it is. That statement is a technical truth. There is not a verse of scripture that has those exact words. There is also no scripture that says, for instance, do not look at internet porn. We know there are verse about living lives that are circumspect from the world, about keeping oneself pure and unstained, and one statement from Jesus specfically that says if a man looks at a woman with lustful intent he has committed adultery with her already in his heart (sermon on the mount, Matthew 5:28 ). The internet as we know it did not exist before 1993 but when we take counsel from the whole of scripture it becomes clear that pornography is not God’s will. Now let’s talk about church. posts.title: Jesus is More
posts.description: I saw this question while scrolling Facebook the other day. The one I saw actually asked about Jesus Christ which I think gives something away. Christ is not a last name; it is the New Testament Greek equivalent of the Hebew word Messiah. It also troubles me a little that the question is not simply Who is Jesus but includes a very personal prepositional phrase: to you . I replied that I like what Peter said when asked by Jesus himself in Matthew 16 : “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.” Calling him Christ acknowledges him as the one they have been waiting for. Matthew, if you recall, quoted Isaiah 7 back in chapter 1 when citing the birth of Jesus as the fulfillment of prophecy. Calling him the Son of God – the living God – distinguishes Jesus from the many false messiahs that came before and after. In short, Peter was saying that Jesus was exactly what they had been waiting for, the fulfillment of biblical prophecy. The disciples were putting all of their eggs in one baske

posts.title: Is the Bible Anti-women? Part 2
posts.description: In Genesis 2 God said that it was not good for man to be alone and then created the very first woman. If all people, men and women, would listen to God and make every effort to live out his plan for their lives, that would solve most of our problems. I’m talking about big things – war, food scarcity, sex trafficking – but also the little things – couples that argue over household budgets and whether or not the toilet seat should be left up or put down. If each Christian, regardless of what the rest of the world is doing, would read the Bible and pray, seek God’s will and let the Holy Spirit lead – put pride and ego aside and work together as the Spirit leads – then we could still know peace on a personal level. If only, right? That intro almost turned into its own sermon. Let’s look at this passage from Matthew 23: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, the city that kills the prophets and stones those who are sent to it!
